headline: Neighbourhood Residents’ Welfare Association Demands Formal Bilateral Visa Stamping For Delivery Drivers Crossing Into Different Residential Blocks
body:
"Ever since the new RWA directive, I’ve had to fill out a 12-page diplomatic immunity form just to get my parcel from the gate to the third floor," said local resident Arjun Mehra.

"The delivery app literally asked me to upload a scanned copy of my passport and a formal invitation letter from the neighbor just to deliver a cold latte across the complex divider," complained delivery partner Vikram Singh.

"We are just trying to maintain the sovereignty of our block, and honestly, the diplomatic protocol of serving iced tea before asking for the parcel ID is a matter of basic international etiquette," explained RWA secretary Mrs. Chatterjee.

"My son is currently studying political science, and he spent his entire weekend acting as a neutral mediator to ensure the packet of namkeen didn't trigger a full-scale trade war between the two blocks," added homemaker Sunita Rao.

"At this point, I think I’ll just start air-dropping my grocery orders via drone, as the visa processing fee for the security guard to cross the median strip is becoming cost-prohibitive," noted software engineer Rahul Verma.
caption: Diplomacy begins at the gate! Our RWA has officially turned the apartment complex into the UN headquarters. If you need a visa to get your Zomato order, you’re not alone. #RWA #Diplomacy #ApartmentLife #DeliveryWoes (satire)
igHook: Would you pay a visa fee to get your food delivered to your door?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a modern apartment complex gate with a makeshift wooden barrier and a security guard holding a clipboard, looking confused at a delivery driver.

sourceHeadline.title: After brief disruption, officials restart talks for Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman’s India visit

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 12 stands out by applying the 'diplomatic protocol' premise to the highly specific, relatable, and localized context of RWA (Residential Welfare Association) squabbles. It avoids the repetitive 'traffic jam' trope found in almost all other candidates and creates a genuinely funny, warm observation about bureaucratic creep in daily life.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses fictional characters and a satirical premise to poke fun at overzealous Resident Welfare Associations. It does not name real public or private individuals, nor does it touch upon sensitive social, religious, or ethnic topics. The image prompt is generic and avoids identifiable people or brands.
